data.hypothesis: Packing short H rows into each CTA should reduce CTA overhead and inactive threads in the separate forward and input-gradient passes. The mapping uses row_width=min(L,256) and packs floor(256/row_width) rows per CTA; for L=48, this assigns five rows to a 240-thread CTA instead of launching one 256-thread CTA per row. Rows of length at least 256 retain the existing one-row, 256-thread mapping. The baseline is correct at 35.464 ms mean for the full call, but it does not isolate these kernels; any benefit remains unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use full-call timing to assess mapping changes; the baseline's combined time cannot establish the contribution of either pass.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline passed all eight reported correctness cases and measured 35.464 ms mean across three samples, but that measurement combines the full call and does not attribute time to individual kernels.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this candidate with the controller's correctness checks and full-call timing.

data.notes: Forward and input-gradient remain separate. Each valid (b,h,t) output retains the original FP32 accumulation and bounds checks, with one thread writing each output; the weight-gradient kernel is unchanged. No candidate correctness or timing result is available yet.
transformations: Map each forward and input-gradient CTA across multiple H rows when L is below 256: block.x is L and block.y is floor(256/L), with a bounds guard for incomplete H groups.
Keep 256-wide x tiles and one row per CTA for L >= 256, preserving the existing per-row output mapping for longer rows.
Retain the separate FP32 forward and input-gradient passes, their bounds-safe zero padding and complete writes; leave the weight-gradient kernel unchanged.
